title: Drive unit temperature warning
shortDescription: The motor is hot; output is reduced.
fullDescription:
W010 is a warning that the Shimano STEPS drive unit has reached a high temperature threshold. The system reduces assist to protect internal components until the motor cools.

Stop pedaling uphill under maximum assist and let the motor cool. The code clears automatically once temperature drops.

fixSteps.title: Stop and cool
fixSteps.instruction: Pause for 5-10 minutes in shade so the motor can cool.

fixSteps.title: Use lower assist modes
fixSteps.instruction: Continue in ECO or TRAIL mode to limit heat buildup.

whenToCallPro: If the warning appears even under light use.

faq.a: No, it self-clears once the motor cools.

title: Battery temperature warning
shortDescription: Battery temperature is outside the optimal range.
fullDescription:
W011 warns that the battery is hotter or colder than recommended. Performance is reduced until the battery returns to its normal operating range.

Avoid charging a very cold battery; let it warm up first.

fixSteps.title: Rest battery
fixSteps.instruction: Let battery reach 15-25 C before continuing.

whenToCallPro: If warning persists in moderate conditions.

faq.q: Can I store battery in cold garage?

title: Torque sensor warning
shortDescription: Torque sensor may not be calibrated correctly.
fullDescription:
W013 indicates that the torque sensor in the drive unit reported a zero offset that is out of tolerance. Often appears the first time the bike is powered on while someone is standing on the pedals.

Restart the system with no load on the pedals.

fixSteps.title: Restart without load
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off system, ensure no weight is on pedals, turn on again.

fixSteps.title: Dealer calibration
fixSteps.instruction: If warning persists, have the torque sensor recalibrated via E-Tube.

whenToCallPro: If restart does not clear the warning.

title: Firmware mismatch warning
shortDescription: Component firmware versions do not match.
fullDescription:
W103 appears when the drive unit, display, or battery have different firmware versions that are not fully compatible. The bike may still ride, but features may be limited.

Update all components with Shimano E-Tube software at a dealer.

fixSteps.title: E-Tube update
fixSteps.instruction: Visit dealer or use E-Tube Project/PC to update all firmware.

whenToCallPro: To perform the update at a Shimano dealer.

title: Incompatible component warning
fullDescription:
W104 is shown when the system detects a connected component that is not part of the approved compatibility list, for example an older display on a newer drive unit.

Replace with a compatible component or have dealer verify.

fixSteps.title: Verify compatibility
fixSteps.instruction: Check Shimano compatibility chart for your drive unit.

faq.a: Generally no, but features may be limited.

title: Battery low capacity warning
shortDescription: Battery has degraded and can no longer hold normal capacity.
fullDescription:
W105 indicates that the battery pack has reached a degradation threshold where usable capacity is significantly reduced. Typically appears after years of use or many charge cycles.

Consider replacement for continued long rides.

fixSteps.title: Battery capacity check
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer E-Tube can report actual capacity percentage.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new compatible Shimano battery if capacity is too low.

title: Drive unit system error
shortDescription: A serious system error has been detected.
fullDescription:
E010 is a critical error that indicates internal failure or a firmware issue in the STEPS drive unit. Motor assist is disabled.

Reboot the system. If the error persists, a dealer must inspect the drive unit with E-Tube diagnostics.

fixSteps.title: Reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery, wait 30 seconds, reinsert and power on.

fixSteps.title: Dealer diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, visit Shimano dealer for E-Tube diagnostic.

whenToCallPro: If reboot does not clear the error.

faq.a: Yes, the bike is still a bicycle.

title: Speed sensor error
shortDescription: Speed sensor signal is missing or wrong.
fullDescription:
E014 indicates that the drive unit cannot read the speed sensor correctly. Like on other systems, this is usually a spoke magnet alignment issue.

Confirm the magnet lines up with the sensor on the chainstay and the gap is correct.

fixSteps.title: Align magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Set spoke magnet so it passes within 5-8 mm of sensor.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect sensor for cracks or impact damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new Shimano speed sensor if damaged.

whenToCallPro: If replacement does not resolve it.

faq.q: Can I use a non-Shimano magnet?

title: Battery communication error
shortDescription: Drive unit cannot communicate with the battery.
fullDescription:
E020 appears when the battery is unreachable on the system bus. Causes include a dirty battery contact, a loose cable, or a fault in the battery BMS.

Remove battery, clean contacts, and reseat firmly.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Clean battery and frame contacts with contact cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Reseat battery
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall battery, ensure it clicks into place.

fixSteps.title: Dealer diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: If error continues, dealer must test battery and wiring.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning and reseating do not help.

faq.a: Not necessarily, often just a contact issue.

title: Incompatible battery
fullDescription:
E021 indicates the connected battery is not approved for this drive unit. Installing an older or mismatched Shimano battery is the most common cause.

Use a battery listed as compatible with your STEPS generation.

fixSteps.title: Check compatibility
fixSteps.instruction: Consult Shimano compatibility chart for your drive unit.

title: Battery internal error
fullDescription:
E022 is set by the battery BMS when it detects an internal problem such as a voltage imbalance or temperature sensor failure. The battery is disabled for safety.

Do not open the battery. Have it tested by a dealer.

fixSteps.title: Rest and recharge
fixSteps.instruction: Let battery sit for a few hours then attempt charging.

fixSteps.title: Dealer test
fixSteps.instruction: If error returns, take battery to Shimano dealer.

whenToCallPro: If error persists after rest and recharge.

faq.a: Only if not swollen, leaking, or hot.

title: Battery charge fault
fullDescription:
E023 is reported when a charging session ended with an error, such as overvoltage, undervoltage, or communication loss to the charger. Often clears after a successful charge attempt.

Use only a genuine Shimano charger and inspect the cable.

fixSteps.title: Retry charge
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug charger, wait 60 seconds, try again.

fixSteps.title: Replace charger
fixSteps.instruction: If charger is suspect, replace with genuine Shimano charger.

whenToCallPro: If new charger does not resolve.

faq.q: Can a power outage cause this?
faq.a: Yes, it is a common trigger.
